name: Normandy Tribunal
description: Hermetic Tribunal covering northern France from the Atlantic to Lorraine and south to the River Dordogne, with many small covenants and scarce vis; formerly the Tribunal of the West Franks.

name: Rhine Tribunal
description: Neighboring Tribunal to the east of Normandy; one of the original Tribunals created in 865.

name: Greater Alps Tribunal
description: Tribunal bordering the Normandy Tribunal to the east.

name: Provençal Tribunal
description: Tribunal to the south of Normandy, bordered at the River Dordogne; its border with Normandy is decided on linguistic grounds (langue d'oc vs langue d'oeil).

name: Lotharingian Tribunal
description: Original Tribunal created in 865 covering the kingdom of Lotharingia; dissolved in 898, and some covenants now seek its restoration.

name: Britannian Tribunal
description: Original Tribunal that initially included Brittany; later divided into the Stonehenge, Loch Leglean, and Hibernian Tribunals.

name: Stonehenge Tribunal
description: One of the Tribunals into which the Britannian Tribunal later divided.

name: Loch Leglean Tribunal
description: One of the Tribunals formed from the division of the Britannian Tribunal.

name: Hibernian Tribunal
description: One of the Tribunals formed from the division of the Britannian Tribunal.

name: Roman Tribunal
description: One of the original Tribunals created in 865, which ruled the Italian part of Lotharingia.

name: Theban Tribunal
description: One of the original Tribunals created in 865.

name: Sanctuary of the Alps
description: One of the original Tribunals created at the Second Grand Tribunal in 865.

name: Grand Tribunal
description: Order-wide Tribunal meeting; the second Grand Tribunal in 865 created the regional Tribunals and confirmed Peripheral Code rights.

name: House Tytalus
description: Hermetic House whose domus magna, Fudarus, is in the Normandy Tribunal; drawn to the region's conflict and suffered a Corruption in the late ninth century.

name: House Diedne
description: Pagan Hermetic House, possibly descended from the druids, prominent in Brittany and Normandy until destroyed in the Schism War.

name: House Flambeau
description: Hermetic House that fought the Diedne and quarreled with Tytalus over Diedne vis sources; many members admire tales of Roland and El Cid.

name: House Mercere
description: Hermetic House of Redcaps that proposed regional Redcap networks leading to Tribunals; its bloodline is the best-known mythic lineage.

name: House Guernicus
description: Hermetic House of Quaesitores whose censors are believed to have excised Diedne records.

name: House Tremere
description: Hermetic House rumored to have been slowed by, or to have planned, the 865 partitioning of the Order.

name: House Jerbiton
description: Hermetic House; Metrodorus of Thebes and Adela were Jerbiton magi.

name: House Merinita
description: Hermetic House; one Merinita magus moved a hill to alter a seisin claim.

name: House Bonisagus
description: Hermetic House of Perpauca Bonisagi.

name: House Criamon
description: Hermetic House of Hicuccus, author of The Babble Within Thought.

name: House Ex Miscellanea
description: Hermetic House into which the Donatores Requietis Aeternae tradition was inducted.

name: Order of Hermes
description: The organization of Hermetic magi, whose members in Normandy adapt closely to mundane society.

name: Order of Odin
description: Feared Scandinavian parallel to the Order of Hermes, supposedly of rune-wielding Gifted shape-changers who led Viking raids.

name: Quaesitores
description: Hermetic investigators and judges who watch inquiries into the Schism War and adjudicate vis claims and leases.

name: Redcaps
description: Mercere messengers whose network was organized regionally; their vis trading is exempt from the Perthean Compact.

name: Magvillus
description: Covenant to which Quaesitor Lothaire was invited in recognition of his long service.

name: Fudarus
description: Island covenant in Brittany, domus magna of House Tytalus; the only surviving Breton covenant after the Schism War and a powerful liege covenant.

name: Confluensis
description: Covenant that keeps the Tribunal's library and the public record of luctationes; formerly sited at Dragon's Rest.

name: Dragon's Rest
description: Site at the mouth of the Seine, raided many times by Vikings, formerly the site of Confluensis covenant.

name: Baiocassium
description: Diedne-dominated covenant near Bayeux, raided by Vikings, destroyed in the Schism War after destroying Pagus.

name: Kerguntuil
description: Diedne covenant on the Brittany coast raided several times by Vikings.

name: Montverte
description: Covenant established by Scandinavian converts to the Order; derives mundane resources from raiding nearby covenants.

name: Pagus
description: Covenant near Cherbourg heavily raided by Vikings and destroyed by Baiocassium during the Schism War.

name: Rotomagus
description: Young covenant near Rouen destroyed in Viking raids.

name: Florum
description: Urban covenant (Conventio Florum) near Ghent, once at Spider's Palace, ordered to dismantle its magical linen factory in 1081.

name: Spider's Palace
description: Site raided several times by Vikings, then home to the newly founded Florum covenant.

name: Branugurix
description: Great House Diedne covenant in a regio whose entrances were sealed when attacked in the Schism War.

name: Lapis Crudus
description: Covenant which reappeared after being trapped for decades in a regio; victim of Koilios's raid in 1113.

name: Atramentum
description: Vassal covenant of Fudarus whose magi were ruined by guild politics in Le Conquet and later evicted.

name: Praeda
description: Covenant running an auction of vis smuggled from southern Tribunals, contrary to the Perthean Compact.

name: Bibracte
description: Covenant present at the inaugural meeting of the Tribunal of the West Franks in 871.

name: Sinapis
description: Covenant present at the inaugural meeting of the Tribunal of the West Franks in 871.

name: Nauche-Fleur
description: Covenant accused in 1095 of feudal obligation to a baron via an unGifted companion; found innocent.

name: Infelicitas
description: Covenant raided by Jacinth of Oleron, whose upper story collapsed destroying two laboratories.

name: Oleron
description: Normandy covenant of Jacinth of Oleron.

name: Fengheld
description: Rhine Tribunal covenant with a chapter house in Cherbourg, considered a coenobium by Normandy.

name: Nidi
description: Covenant described in the Anjou and Aquitaine chapter.

name: Atsingani
description: Covenant described in the Anjou and Aquitaine chapter.

name: Eboris
description: Covenant in the Ile de France.

name: Requies Aeterna
description: Covenant in Picardy.

name: Cunfin
description: Covenant in Champagne.

name: Exspectatio
description: Covenant in Brittany.

name: Lotharingian Movement
description: Group of covenants seeking to secede from Normandy and the Rhine to reform the Lotharingian Tribunal.

name: Apple Guild
description: Rhine Tribunal guild with which the Lotharingians sympathize.

name: Donatores Requietis Aeternae
description: Ex Miscellanea tradition of hedge wizards who fought restless dead, inducted by Quaesitor Muirgheal in 1109.

name: Northern Tytali
description: Tytalus faction in the post-Schism Normandy Tribunal opposed to the Southern Flambeau.

name: Southern Flambeau
description: Flambeau faction that opposed the Tytali over Diedne spoils; three covenants defected to Provence.

name: Cabal of Frankish Gold
description: Cabal described in the Normandy Sagas chapter.

name: Cabal of the Laden Cart
description: Tytalus scheme cabal described in the Normandy Sagas chapter.

name: Cabal of the Crushed Viper
description: Tytalus scheme cabal described in the Normandy Sagas chapter.

name: Druids
description: Pagan priests of the Gauls, possibly precursors of House Diedne.

name: Merovingian Dynasty
description: First Frankish royal dynasty, descended from Merovech; its sorcerer-kings kept magic in their long hair.

name: Carolingian Dynasty
description: Frankish dynasty named after Charlemagne; its blood often carries the Mythic Presence Virtue.

name: Capetian Dynasty
description: French royal dynasty descended from Hugh Capet, noted for piety, symbolized by gold lilies on blue.

name: Angevin Dynasty
description: Dynasty of Anjou ruling England and Aquitaine, symbolized by three gold lions; legendarily descended from Melusine.

name: Franks
description: Germanic tribal grouping that settled Gaul and founded the Merovingian kingdom.

name: Gauls
description: Ancient inhabitants of the region who revered the boar and sacrificed to spirits and faeries.

name: Vikings
description: Scandinavian raiders who ravaged France and Hermetic covenants in the 9th-10th centuries and settled Normandy.

name: Cathars
description: Heretics of the Langue d'oc targeted by the Albigensian Crusade.

name: Trouvères
description: Wandering French poets who sing tales of romance and Arthurian legend.

name: Philip II Augustus
description: King of France in 1220, the seventh Capetian, with the Royal Touch; conquered Normandy from John.

name: Saint Denis
description: Third-century missionary to Paris beheaded at Montmartre; patron saint of France.

name: Eleutherius
description: Assistant of St. Denis, martyred with him.

name: Rusticus
description: Assistant of St. Denis, martyred with him.

name: Julius Caesar
description: Roman general who conquered the Gauls and wrote about them.

name: Gregory of Tours
description: Historian whose Decem Libri Historiarum records the Frankish kings.

name: Vercingetorix
description: Gaulish king defeated by Caesar at Alesia.

name: King Arthur
description: Legendary British king whose kingdom's collapse drove Celts to Brittany.

name: Childeric
description: Frankish king who assisted Rome against the Visigoths.

name: Clovis
description: Merovingian king (481-511) who converted after victory over the Alemanni and was anointed with the Holy Oil.

name: Syagrius
description: Roman governor defeated by Clovis in 486.

name: Clotilde of Burgundy
description: Christian wife of Clovis whose prayers cured their son.

name: Saint Martin of Tours
description: Saint at whose tomb a miracle swayed Clovis.

name: Vedast
description: Bishop of Arras who restored a blind man's sight.

name: Saint Rémi
description: Archbishop of Reims who baptized and anointed Clovis; possible source of the Royal Touch.

name: Dagobert I
description: Merovingian king (603-639) who unified and conquered.

name: Charles Martel
description: Frankish hero who won the Battle of Poitiers in 732.

name: Pépin
description: Son of Charles Martel who seized the throne from the Merovingians in 754.

name: Merovech
description: Progenitor of the Merovingians, born of a Frankish queen and a beast like the Quinotaur.

name: Duke Francio
description: Legendary ancestor of the Frankish kings who fought alongside Priam at Troy.

name: King Clodio
description: King of the Franks whose wife bore Merovech.

name: Blitild
description: Daughter of King Clothar claimed as ancestor by the Carolingians.

name: Pope Stephen II
description: Pope who in 754 decreed excommunication for making non-Carolingian kings.

name: Charlemagne
description: Carolingian emperor and King of France, hero of the Epic of Charlemagne.

name: Alcuin
description: British priest and scholar, adviser to Charlemagne.

name: Roland
description: Paladin of Charlemagne slain at Roncesvalles; admired by Flambeau magi.

name: Hugh Capet
description: Founder of the Capetian dynasty, King of the Franks from 987.

name: Robert the Strong
description: Ninth-century ancestor of Hugh Capet.

name: Hugh the Great
description: Effective ruler of France under weak Carolingian kings.

name: Gerbert of Aurilliac
description: Scholar with reputed minor magical talent who aided Hugh Capet; archbishop of Reims.

name: Saint Valéry
description: Saint whose body Hugh Capet recovered.

name: Saint Riquier
description: Saint whose body Hugh Capet recovered.

name: Prince Louis
description: Heir of Philip Augustus, born 1187, not yet anointed; invaded England in 1216.

name: Rollo
description: Viking leader granted Rouen in 911, ancestor of the dukes of Normandy.

name: Charles III
description: French king who made an accord with Rollo in 911.

name: William the Bastard
description: Rollo's successor who conquered England in 1066.

name: Henry II
description: King of England, Duke of Normandy and Aquitaine and Count of Anjou; husband of Eleanor.

name: Richard the Lionheart
description: Angevin King of England who warred with Philip and died at Chalus in 1199.

name: King John
description: Angevin King of England who lost Normandy and possibly murdered Arthur of Brittany.

name: Henry III
description: Boy king of England in 1220 and Norman claimant to the duchy.

name: Eleanor of Aquitaine
description: Duchess who married Louis VII then Henry II, mother of Richard and John.

name: Louis VII
description: King of France, first husband of Eleanor, father of Philip Augustus.

name: Louis VI
description: King of France who died in 1137.

name: Duke William of Aquitaine
description: Father of Eleanor who died on pilgrimage in 1137.

name: Raymond of Poitiers
description: Ruler of Antioch, Eleanor's uncle, rumored lover.

name: Melusine
description: Faerie or demon maiden who married a lord of Anjou and fled Mass; ancestress of the Angevins.

name: Adèle of Champagne
description: Third wife of Louis VII and mother of Philip Augustus.

name: Isabella of Hainault
description: First wife of Philip Augustus and mother of Louis.

name: Agnès of Méranie
description: Third wife of Philip Augustus.

name: Henry the Young King
description: Eldest son of Henry II, crowned in his father's lifetime, died 1183.

name: Geoffrey of Brittany
description: Son of Henry II, died 1186, father of Arthur of Brittany.

name: Duke Leopold of Austria
description: Duke insulted by Richard on crusade who imprisoned him.

name: Saladin
description: Muslim leader against whom Richard crusaded.

name: Arthur of Brittany
description: Son of Geoffrey with a strong claim to England; vanished at Rouen in 1203, rumored to be Gifted and apprenticed.

name: William the Marshall
description: Trusted friend of Richard.

name: Constance of Brittany
description: Widow of Geoffrey and mother of Arthur of Brittany.

name: Isabella of Angouleme
description: Wife of King John, suspected of bewitching him.

name: Hugh de Lusignan
description: Angevin vassal betrothed to Isabella of Angouleme.

name: Bertram de Gurdun
description: Crossbowman who shot Richard at Chalus.

name: Mercadier
description: Mercenary knight who botched Richard's wound and flayed Bertram.

name: William de Braose
description: Jailer of Arthur of Brittany.

name: King Lothair
description: King of Lotharingia whose kingdom split in 855.

name: Lothair II
description: King of Lotharingia who died without heir in 869.

name: Charles the Bald
description: King of West Francia who acknowledged Breton independence.

name: Louis the German
description: King of East Francia who divided Lotharingia at Meersen.

name: Merlin
description: Legendary figure whose stories shaped the magical heritage of Brittany.

name: Adrianus of Montverte
description: Magus who proposed renaming the Tribunal of the West Franks as Normandy in 983.

name: Pertheus of Tytalus
description: Tytalus magus who drafted the Perthean Compact.

name: Metrodorus of Thebes
description: Jerbiton Quaesitor who originated the mythic bloodline theory and was Marched.

name: Barnabé
description: Arrogant grog cursor trained to run for seisin trials.

name: Perpauca Bonisagi
description: Hermetic author who began donating books to the Tribunal library.

name: Quaesitor Celestin
description: Quaesitor who ruled mundane resources do not contribute to magical power.

name: Koilios
description: Tytalus magus who raided Lapis Crudus in 1113.

name: Hicuccus of Criamon
description: Author of The Babble Within Thought.

name: Azenis of Tytalus
description: Author of The Dismal Itch.

name: Jeremias filius Guernicus
description: Author of De Lapii.

name: Adanos Lutorum of Tytalus
description: Author of The Mole's Work.

name: Peter of Uist
description: Author of The Primal Power.

name: Notatus
description: Co-author of Research Notes on Aegis of the Hearth.

name: Jacinda of Flambeau
description: Author of Subtle Knives.

name: Daniel Tonatris
description: Author of Unveiling the Tempest.

name: Quaesitor Fluvius
description: Quaesitor who wrote The Order and Towns and invented An Ear for Distant Bells.

name: Adela of Jerbiton
description: Maga acquitted in 885 of acting as court wizard to Louis III.

name: Louis III
description: King to whom Adela was accused of being court wizard.

name: Quaesitor Muirgheal
description: Quaesitor who inducted the Donatores Requietis Aeternae in 1109.

name: Quaesitor Lothaire
description: Chief Quaesitor of Normandy who permitted mundane raiding; later joined Magvillus.

name: Praecepsus of Flambeau
description: Magus accused of using a Perdo-enchanted sword in 1111.

name: Pandion of Flambeau
description: Magus convicted of stealing a magical horse from a Redcap.

name: Antonin of Dragon's Rest
description: Redcap robbed of horses by Pandion.

name: Jacinth of Oleron
description: Magus convicted of damaging Infelicitas; later accused Lothaire of partisanship.

name: Atlax of Tytalus
description: Fudarus magus who read the Redcap Camille's messages.

name: Camille of Mercere
description: Redcap whose messages were read; later fined for using a knight to harvest vis.

name: Quaesitor Whent
description: Quaesitor who stripped Fudarus of a legacy lease in 1172.

name: Pernix of Merinita
description: Magus acquitted of healing a nobleman with magic in 1179.

name: Visurgis of Tytalus
description: Magus who accused Pernix of interfering with mundanes.

name: Buliste of Tytalus
description: Magus who accused Camille of interfering with mundanes.

name: Pugnatis
description: Maga convicted of controlling the mayor of Laval and expelled in 1207.

name: Zeus
description: Pagan god whose bull-form is linked to the Quinotaur.

name: Europa
description: Phoenician princess carried off by Zeus.

name: Poseidon
description: Pagan god associated with the Quinotaur and Atlantis.

name: King Priam
description: King of Troy alongside whom Duke Francio fought.

name: El Cid
description: Iberian hero whose tales Flambeau magi love.

name: Quinotaur
description: Supernatural creature with the fore parts of a bull and the hind of a great fish, a Magic creature of the Atlantic said to be ancestor of the Merovingians.

name: Leviathan
description: Sea monster to which some link the Quinotaur.

name: Giants
description: Beings who followed the elemental spirits and left megaliths across France.

name: Elemental spirits
description: Primordial spirits of fire and water that retreated underground, revealed in hot and cold springs.

name: Faeries
description: Supernatural folk that control many Norman forests.

name: Demons
description: Infernal beings imprisoned by saints and sorcerers in Normandy.

name: Angels
description: Divine beings who fought over human souls.

name: Basilisk
description: Creature nesting under a tree whose fruit is Perdo vis in an example luctatio.

name: Ghostly maiden
description: Ghost whose lament is Mentem vis.

name: Restless dead
description: Undead plague fought by the Donatores Requietis Aeternae.

name: Holy Oil of Consecration
description: Ampoule of never-ending oil brought by a dove at Clovis's baptism, used to anoint French kings; a 3-point relic in Reims Cathedral.

name: Treasure of Chalus
description: Golden treasure found at Chalus that lured Richard to his death; possibly diabolical.

name: The Babble Within Thought
description: Summa on Mentem by Hicuccus of Criamon owned by the Tribunal.

name: The Dismal Itch
description: Summa on Corpus by Azenis of Tytalus.

name: De Lapii
description: Summa on Terram by Jeremias filius Guernicus.

name: Insights from Twilight
description: Summa on Magic Theory by Perpauca Bonisagi.

name: Mirrors of the Soul
description: Summa on Imaginem by Perpauca Bonisagi.

name: The Mole's Work
description: Lab texts by Adanos Lutorum of Tytalus.

name: The Peril of Phoebos
description: Tractatus on Ignem by Perpauca Bonisagi.

name: The Primal Power
description: Summa on Aquam by Peter of Uist.

name: Research Notes on Aegis of the Hearth
description: Tractatus with a lab text of Aegis of the Hearth.

name: Subtle Knives
description: Summa on Penetration by Jacinda of Flambeau.

name: Unveiling the Tempest
description: Summa on Auram by Daniel Tonatris.

name: The Order and Towns
description: Code of Hermes summa by Quaesitor Fluvius (1208) on mundane interactions.

name: Decem Libri Historiarum
description: Gregory of Tours' history of the Frankish kings.

name: Epic of Charlemagne
description: Collection of chivalric tales about Charlemagne and his paladins.

name: An Ear for Distant Bells
description: InIm 15 spell to determine the distance and direction to a sound's source; invented by Quaesitor Fluvius.

name: Rock of Viscid Clay
description: Spell with a lab text in The Mole's Work.

name: Earth That Breaks No More
description: Spell with a lab text in The Mole's Work.

name: The Forgiving Earth
description: Spell with a lab text in The Mole's Work.

name: Aegis of the Hearth
description: Spell subject of research notes and a lab text in the Tribunal library.

name: Seven League Stride
description: Spell used to define that council chambers must be out of range of each other.

name: Aura of Rightful Authority
description: Effect equivalent granted by coronation's Commanding Aura.

name: Aura of Enobled Presence
description: Effect wrongly believed bestowed permanently by the Holy Oil.

name: Greater Immunity
description: Major Supernatural Virtue (Drowning) common among Merovech's descendants.

name: Royal Touch
description: Power of French kings to cure the King's Evil, possibly from the Holy Oil or Merovech.

name: Purifying Touch
description: Virtue some believe underlies the Royal Touch.

name: True Faith
description: Virtue manifested by some Capetians.

name: Mythic Presence
description: Virtue often held by those of Carolingian blood.

name: Mythic Blood
description: Virtue of magical bloodline; some theorists claim all magi carry it.

name: The Gift
description: Innate magical talent, thought by some theorists to be latent Mythic Blood.

name: Personal Vis Source
description: Hermetic Virtue whose vis, if generated by the magus's person, is exempt from the Perthean Compact.

name: Enduring Constitution
description: Virtue of Barnabé.

name: Improved Characteristics
description: Virtue of Barnabé.

name: Puissant Athletics
description: Virtue of Barnabé.

name: Covenant Upbringing
description: Flaw of Barnabé.

name: Proud
description: Minor Flaw of Barnabé.

name: Social Handicap
description: Flaw of Barnabé (arrogance).

name: Disfigured
description: Flaw acquired by advanced scrofula sufferers.

name: Dark Secret
description: Flaw that could pair with plundering an undisclosed vis source.

name: Medicine
description: Ability referenced in the text (e.g. in Barnabé's statistics or the Tribunal library).

name: Athletics
description: Ability referenced in the text (e.g. in Barnabé's statistics or the Tribunal library).

name: Area Lore
description: Ability referenced in the text (e.g. in Barnabé's statistics or the Tribunal library).

name: Carouse
description: Ability referenced in the text (e.g. in Barnabé's statistics or the Tribunal library).

name: Awareness
description: Ability referenced in the text (e.g. in Barnabé's statistics or the Tribunal library).

name: Brawl
description: Ability referenced in the text (e.g. in Barnabé's statistics or the Tribunal library).

name: Folk Ken
description: Ability referenced in the text (e.g. in Barnabé's statistics or the Tribunal library).

name: French
description: Ability referenced in the text (e.g. in Barnabé's statistics or the Tribunal library).

name: Guile
description: Ability referenced in the text (e.g. in Barnabé's statistics or the Tribunal library).

name: Latin
description: Ability referenced in the text (e.g. in Barnabé's statistics or the Tribunal library).

name: Order of Hermes Lore
description: Ability referenced in the text (e.g. in Barnabé's statistics or the Tribunal library).

name: Stealth
description: Ability referenced in the text (e.g. in Barnabé's statistics or the Tribunal library).

name: Survival
description: Ability referenced in the text (e.g. in Barnabé's statistics or the Tribunal library).

description: Ability referenced in the text (e.g. in Barnabé's statistics or the Tribunal library).

name: Penetration
description: Ability referenced in the text (e.g. in Barnabé's statistics or the Tribunal library).

name: Code of Hermes
description: Ability referenced in the text (e.g. in Barnabé's statistics or the Tribunal library).

name: Creo
description: Hermetic Art referenced as vis type, spell Art, or book subject.

name: Corpus
description: Hermetic Art referenced as vis type, spell Art, or book subject.

name: Mentem
description: Hermetic Art referenced as vis type, spell Art, or book subject.

name: Terram
description: Hermetic Art referenced as vis type, spell Art, or book subject.

name: Imaginem
description: Hermetic Art referenced as vis type, spell Art, or book subject.

name: Ignem
description: Hermetic Art referenced as vis type, spell Art, or book subject.

name: Aquam
description: Hermetic Art referenced as vis type, spell Art, or book subject.

name: Auram
description: Hermetic Art referenced as vis type, spell Art, or book subject.

name: Intellego
description: Hermetic Art referenced as vis type, spell Art, or book subject.

name: Perdo
description: Hermetic Art referenced as vis type, spell Art, or book subject.

name: Animal
description: Hermetic Art referenced as vis type, spell Art, or book subject.

name: Vim
description: Hermetic Art referenced as vis type, spell Art, or book subject.

name: Perthean Compact
description: Normandy Peripheral Code rulings drafted by Pertheus distributing vis sources as seisins, legacies, tropaea, and luctationes.

name: Seisin
description: Vis source within a day's return march of a covenant's council chamber, belonging to it automatically.

name: Legacy
description: Distant vis source leased to its discoverer by Tribunal vote for seven years.

name: Tropaeum
description: Tribunal-owned easily harvested vis source leased via the Tourney.

name: Luctatio
description: Tribunal-owned vis source whose harvest needs skill, open to any magus.

name: Interim lease
description: Provisional lease on a newly found vis source granted by a Quaesitor.

name: Plundering
description: Low Crime of harvesting an undeclared vis source without an interim lease.

name: Cursor
description: Athletic grog who proves in a trial run that a vis source is a seisin.

name: Council chamber
description: Official meeting place of a covenant used to measure seisins and covenant spacing.

name: Hermetic Tourney
description: Seven-yearly tournament in which Normandy covenants compete for vis leases and books.

name: Library of the Normandy Tribunal
description: Tribunal-owned book collection kept at Confluensis and leased as Tourney prizes.

name: Town Senex
description: Covenant closest to a town (by loudest church bells) with superior rights there.

name: Masks
description: Mundane allies through which covenants act to avoid charges of meddling.

name: Magus errant
description: Tradition of young magi adventuring abroad for vis and renown.

name: Liege and Vassal Covenants
description: Feudal hierarchy of covenants with oaths of fealty and duties of service and protection.

name: Chapter house
description: Remote covenant site prohibited from sidestepping the Perthean Compact.

name: Coenobium
description: Normandy classification for Fengheld's Cherbourg chapter house.

name: Peripheral Code
description: Tribunal-specific law binding only within its own Tribunal.

name: Schism War
description: Hermetic war that destroyed House Diedne, with terrible clashes in Normandy and Brittany.

name: Corruption of House Tytalus
description: Late ninth-century corruption or betrayal of House Tytalus.

name: Wizard's March
description: Hermetic sentence of death and outlawry.

name: Wizard War
description: Sanctioned Hermetic feud threatened by Fudarus.

name: High Crime of depriving a magus of his magical power
description: Crime committed by harvesting another's legacy or damaging magical resources.

name: Meddling with mundanes
description: Code offense interpreted loosely in Normandy as requiring ruin to magi.

name: Certamen
description: Magical duel used to settle library disputes and challenges during raids.

name: Vis
description: Raw magical power, scarce in Normandy.

name: Twilight
description: State into which magi may be lost.

name: Regio
description: Magical layered area; Branugurix and Lapis Crudus were trapped in regiones.

name: Aura
description: Supernatural ambient power; a cave holds a powerful Divine aura.

name: Magic Resistance
description: Resistance granted to anointed kings (10).

name: Arcane Connection
description: Link used to target magic, guarded by magi.

name: Gauntlet
description: Apprentice's final test into magehood.

name: Mystery Cults
description: Cults claiming mythic heritage of magi.
